# Calder Bay council approves $1.8 billion light-rail tunnel in narrow vote

## The vote

- The council voted 7-4 early Wednesday, October 21, to approve a $1.8 billion light-rail tunnel downtown.
- The tunnel is 3.2 miles long, with four underground stations, linking Harbor Point ferry terminal and Eastgate medical district.
- Travel time between them would drop from 38 minutes by bus to 11 minutes by train.
- Mayor Elena Vargas backed the project, which was central to her 2024 campaign.
- Councilwoman Janet Ofori, Derek Huang, Priya Raman and Tom Kessler voted no.
- Council President Luis Moreno voted yes after the regional transit agency capped the city's share of cost overruns at 15 percent.

## How it will be paid for

- Federal government: $720 million, pending a final review expected next spring.
- State: $400 million from a 2022 voter-approved transportation bond.
- Local: $680 million, including about $500 million from a half-cent sales tax and the rest from developer fees near the stations.
- The sales tax was approved by voters in March, 54 to 46 percent, and is expected to raise about $62 million a year.
- The city plans to borrow against that revenue, repaying bonds over 30 years.

## Opposition and concerns

- The Calder Bay Taxpayers Alliance says similar tunnels often run over budget. A 2019 University of Westbrook study found large U.S. rail tunnels exceeded budgets by an average of 44 percent.
- Business owners on Fremont Avenue, where two stations will be built, worry about years of construction. Ana Castillo says her bakery lost nearly a third of its revenue during an 8-month water main project in 2021.
- The council passed an amendment creating a $25 million fund for grants of up to $150,000 to small businesses affected by construction. It passed 10-1.

## Environmental review

- The August final environmental impact statement projects 14,000 fewer daily car trips downtown by 2040.
- It projects a reduction of 31,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions per year at projected ridership.
- Contaminated soil from a former rail yard near Union Street station could add up to $40 million, which is already included in the $1.8 billion estimate.

## Timeline

- Construction begins mid-2027, with tunnel boring starting near Harbor Point.
- The boring machine, built in Germany, is expected to arrive in early 2028.
- Opening is projected for late 2031, or 2032 if federal funding is delayed more than six months.
- Projected ridership: 52,000 weekday riders in the first full year, rising to 78,000 by 2040.

## What comes next

- A funding agreement with the regional transit agency is expected in December.
- The agency's board votes on its share November 14.
- The Taxpayers Alliance is collecting signatures for a measure requiring voter approval for city projects over $500 million. It needs about 18,000 valid signatures by February 1 to qualify for the November 2027 ballot.
- Vargas says voters have already backed the project and would do so again.

# Tierra Alta firma un acuerdo de 2.300 millones de dólares para extraer litio en el salar de Quimal

## Resumen del acuerdo

El gobierno de Tierra Alta firmó el martes un acuerdo con la australiana Southern Lithium y la estatal provincial Recursos Andinos. El proyecto extraerá litio en el salar de Quimal, a 4.000 metros de altura. La inversión prevista es de 2.300 millones de dólares en ocho años.

El gobernador Julián Ferreyra dijo que es "la inversión privada más grande de la historia de la provincia". Afirmó que el proyecto creará 1.200 empleos directos en la construcción y 450 puestos permanentes en operación.

## Términos del acuerdo

- Southern Lithium tendrá el 80 % de la sociedad y Recursos Andinos el 20 %.
- Recursos Andinos no aporta capital; su parte se paga con regalías futuras.
- La provincia cobrará regalías del 3 %, el máximo que permite la ley nacional.
- La empresa pagará 5 millones de dólares anuales a un fondo para comunidades cercanas.
- Deberá contratar al menos 70 % de trabajadores residentes en la provincia.
- Deberá comprar al menos 50 % de insumos a proveedores locales, si hay precio y calidad comparables.
- El contrato tiene una revisión cada cinco años. La ministra Carolina Basualdo dijo que, si el precio del litio sube mucho, la provincia podrá renegociar su parte.

## Producción y mercado

- Desde 2029, la planta producirá 40.000 toneladas anuales de carbonato de litio.
- Según la empresa, a precios actuales eso equivale a unos 600 millones de dólares al año.
- La mayor parte se venderá a fabricantes de baterías de Corea del Sur y Japón.
- El precio del litio cayó cerca de 75 % entre 2022 y 2024, según el director ejecutivo Andrew Pike, quien espera que la demanda de autos eléctricos lo impulse antes de 2030.
- El carbonato se exportará por Antofagasta, Chile, a 620 kilómetros.
- La provincia pavimentará la ruta 52 con un crédito de 90 millones de dólares del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo.

## Agua y comunidades

- La tecnología de extracción directa, según la empresa, usa 60 % menos agua que las piletas de evaporación.
- El estudio de impacto ambiental estima un consumo de 180 litros por segundo de un acuífero que abastece a tres comunidades.
- La Mesa de Comunidades del Salar, que reúne a 11 comunidades kollas, rechazó el acuerdo. Su vocera, Rosa Cruz, dijo que no hubo consulta previa, libre e informada, exigida por el Convenio 169 de la OIT.
- El gobierno provincial dice que hubo 14 reuniones informativas entre marzo y agosto. Basualdo reconoció que no todas las comunidades participaron.
- El hidrólogo Martín Quiroga, de la Universidad Nacional de Tierra Alta, dijo que no hay mediciones confiables sobre la recarga del acuífero. Pidió dos años de monitoreo independiente antes de producir.

## Reacciones políticas

- El bloque opositor pedirá la interpelación de Basualdo. El diputado Hernán Sosa calificó el acuerdo de "entrega" y criticó que el texto se publicara 48 horas antes de la firma.
- La Cámara de Comercio de Tierra Alta apoya el proyecto. Su presidenta, Lucía Vélez, dijo que puede cambiar la economía regional. La provincia tiene una tasa de desempleo de 9,8 %, la más alta del norte del país.
- El intendente de Quimal, Ramón Choque, apoya el proyecto con reservas. Pidió que el 30 % de las regalías quede en los municipios de la zona.

## Próximos pasos

- La Legislatura debe ratificar el acuerdo en 60 días. El oficialismo tiene 19 de 35 bancas, suficientes en principio.
- La construcción comenzaría en el primer semestre de 2027.
- La Mesa de Comunidades presentará un amparo ante la Justicia federal la próxima semana para frenar el proyecto hasta que haya consulta.
- Ferreyra dijo que respetará cualquier decisión judicial y confía en que el proyecto avanzará.

# Calder Bay council approves $1.8 billion light-rail tunnel in narrow vote

CALDER BAY — After a nine-hour meeting, the City Council voted 7-4 early Wednesday to approve a $1.8 billion light-rail tunnel, the largest public works project in the city’s 140-year history.

The 3.2-mile tunnel will link Harbor Point ferry terminal and the Eastgate medical district, with four underground stations. Planners say it will cut travel time from 38 minutes by bus to 11 minutes by train.

## The vote

On October 21, after more than 200 residents signed up to speak, Mayor Elena Vargas called the vote “the moment Calder Bay decided to grow up instead of out.” She made the tunnel the centerpiece of her 2024 campaign.

Councilwoman Janet Ofori and council members Derek Huang, Priya Raman and Tom Kessler voted no. Ofori said the project would “drain money from every neighborhood that will never see a single station.”

The other seven members, including Council President Luis Moreno, voted yes. Moreno said he had been undecided until the final week, when the regional transit agency agreed to cap the city’s share of cost overruns at 15 percent.

## How it will be paid for

The federal government has committed $720 million through its Capital Investment Grants program, pending a final review expected next spring. The state will contribute $400 million from a transportation bond voters approved in 2022.

Local sources will provide the remaining $680 million. About $500 million will come from a half-cent sales tax increase approved by voters in March, 54 to 46 percent. Developer fees for projects within a quarter mile of stations will cover the rest.

Finance Director Carla Mendes said the tax should raise $62 million annually. The city plans to borrow against the revenue and repay bonds over 30 years.

“This is not free money, and nobody should pretend it is,” Mendes said. “But the numbers work if construction stays within the cap.”

## Opposition and concerns

The Calder Bay Taxpayers Alliance, which opposed the March sales tax, warned that tunnels in other cities have exceeded budgets. Director Mark Ellison cited a 2019 University of Westbrook study finding that large U.S. rail tunnels exceeded budgets by an average of 44 percent.

“We are being asked to sign a blank check,” Ellison said. “Fifteen percent is a promise, not a guarantee.”

Fremont Avenue business owners, near two planned stations, worried about years of construction. Ana Castillo, who has run a Fremont bakery for 22 years, said an eight-month water-main replacement in 2021 cost her nearly a third of her revenue. “If eight months nearly closed us, what will four years do?” she asked.

The council passed Councilman Ray Delgado’s amendment 10-1, with Kessler opposed. It creates a $25 million fund for grants of up to $150,000 to small businesses affected by construction.

## Environmental review

The final environmental impact statement, released in August, projects 14,000 fewer daily car trips on downtown streets by 2040 and 31,000 metric tons less carbon dioxide emissions annually once ridership reaches projected levels.

The review found contaminated soil from a former rail yard near Union Street station. Special handling could cost up to $40 million; the transit agency said this is included in the $1.8 billion estimate.

## Timeline

Construction is scheduled to start in mid-2027, with tunnel boring near Harbor Point. Project director Samuel Okafor said the boring machine, being built in Germany, should arrive in early 2028.

Okafor said the line should open in late 2031 if the federal grant is approved on schedule. A funding delay of more than six months would push opening to 2032.

The agency projects 52,000 weekday riders in the first full year, rising to 78,000 by 2040.

## What comes next

The approval allows the city to sign a funding agreement with the regional transit agency, expected in December. The agency board will vote on its share November 14.

Opponents may seek a ballot measure requiring voter approval for city projects over $500 million. Ellison said the Taxpayers Alliance is collecting signatures and needs about 18,000 valid signatures by February 1 to qualify for the November 2027 ballot.

Vargas said she was confident the project would survive a challenge. “People voted for this in March,” she said. “They will vote for it again if they have to.”陪

Pike señaló que el precio del litio cayó un 75 % entre 2022 y 2024, pero prevé que la demanda de autos eléctricos lo impulsará para 2035. El producto se exportará por el puerto de Antofagasta. La provincia pavimentará la ruta 52 con un crédito del BID de 90 millones de dólares.

## El agua, en el centro del debate

El proyecto usará extracción directa de litio, que consume 60 % menos agua que la evaporación. El impacto ambiental estima un consumo de 180 litros por segundo de un acuífero que abastece a tres comunidades. Rosa Cruz, vocera de la Mesa de Comunidades del Salar (11 comunidades kollas), rechazó el acuerdo por falta de consulta previa según el Convenio 169 de la OIT. Basualdo afirmó que hubo 14 reuniones informativas entre marzo y agosto. El hidrólogo Martín Quiroga advirtió que faltan datos de recarga del acuífero y pidió monitoreo independiente por dos años.

## Reacciones políticas

El diputado Hernán Sosa criticó la publicación tardía del texto y pedirá interpelar a Basualdo. Lucía Vélez, presidenta de la Cámara de Comercio, celebró el proyecto citando el desempleo provincial del 9,8 %. El intendente Ramón Choque pidió que el 30 % de las regalías quede en los municipios locales.

## Próximos pasos

La Legislatura debe ratificar el acuerdo en 60 días. El oficialismo tiene 19 de 35 bancas. La construcción iniciaría en el primer semestre de 2027. La Mesa de Comunidades presentará un amparo federal la próxima semana. Ferreyra afirmó que respetará la justicia pero confía en el proyecto.
